title: Third Word Worship And Happiness Sin And Loss The Two Soldiers

questions.question: In the story, what were the two soldiers told to do at the beginning?
questions.answer: They were ordered to travel to a faraway city.

questions.question: What happened on the road as they traveled together?
questions.answer: They came to a place where the road split into two ways.

questions.question: What did the man at the fork say about the road on the right?
questions.answer: He said it usually brought benefit and peace of mind, with no real loss.

questions.question: What did he say about the road on the left?
questions.answer: He said it gave no real benefit, and most people who took it ended up losing.

questions.question: How were the two roads alike?
questions.answer: They were the same in distance.

questions.question: What was one main difference between the two roads?
questions.answer: The left road had no order or authority, but the right road was under discipline and command.

questions.question: What did the travelers on the left road not have to carry?
questions.answer: They did not have to carry supplies or weapons.

questions.question: What did the travelers on the right road have to carry?
questions.answer: They had to carry food supplies and a strong weapon.

questions.question: Why might the left road seem easier at first?
questions.answer: It looked lighter and more comfortable because there was no load to carry.

questions.question: Which soldier made the wise choice?
questions.answer: The soldier who chose the right road did.

questions.question: What burden did the successful soldier carry on his back?
questions.answer: He carried a moderate load of supplies and equipment.

questions.question: What bigger troubles was he saved from inside himself?
questions.answer: He was saved from great fear and from having to depend on other people.

questions.question: Why did the other soldier choose the left road?
questions.answer: He did not want to obey the rules and left the army’s order.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier who left the army’s way?
questions.answer: He traveled in need, afraid of everything, and begging from people.

questions.question: How did the second soldier feel as he continued his trip?
questions.answer: His heart felt tight, and his spirit was weighed down by many fears.

questions.question: What happened when the disobedient soldier finally arrived?
questions.answer: He was punished for rebellion and desertion.

questions.question: How was the obedient soldier’s journey different?
questions.answer: He traveled calmly, without depending on others and without fear.

questions.question: What happened to the obedient soldier when he reached the city?
questions.answer: He received a fitting reward for doing his duty faithfully.

questions.question: Who met the two soldiers when the road split?
questions.answer: A man standing at the fork spoke to them.

questions.question: What kind of information did this man give them?
questions.answer: He explained the results of each road and how they were different.

questions.question: According to him, how often did the right road lead to good results?
questions.answer: Most of the time, with nine out of ten travelers doing well.

questions.question: According to him, how often did the left road lead to loss?
questions.answer: Most of the time, with nine out of ten travelers losing.

questions.question: Did the man say one road was longer than the other?
questions.answer: No. He said they were equal in length.

questions.question: What made the left road attractive on the outside?
questions.answer: It seemed easier because people there carried nothing.

questions.question: Why was that ease misleading?
questions.answer: It only looked comfortable, but it did not lead to real good.

questions.question: What practical items were carried by the soldiers on the right road?
questions.answer: They carried food and a weapon.

questions.question: What does carrying those items show about the right road?
questions.answer: It shows that the road requires preparation, responsibility, and readiness.

questions.question: Which soldier is called fortunate in the story?
questions.answer: The one who chose the right road.

questions.question: What happened to his body compared with his heart and spirit?
questions.answer: His body carried some weight, but his inner self was protected from much heavier troubles.

questions.question: Which soldier is called luckless?
questions.answer: The one who chose the left road.

questions.question: What choice showed his rejection of discipline?
questions.answer: He left military order and went his own way.

questions.question: Even though he carried less on his body, what heavier load did he gain?
questions.answer: He gained deep worry, fear, and dependence on others.

questions.question: What does begging from everyone tell us about his condition?
questions.answer: It shows he became weak, needy, and without dignity.

questions.question: What does trembling before every object and event show?
questions.answer: It shows that he was living in constant fear.

questions.question: What final result came to the disobedient soldier?
questions.answer: He was treated as someone who had rebelled and run away from duty.

questions.question: What qualities did the obedient soldier show?
questions.answer: He respected order, protected his equipment, and stayed loyal to his duty.

questions.question: How did those qualities affect his journey?
questions.answer: They gave him peace, independence, and courage.

questions.question: What two things does the passage compare at the start?
questions.answer: It compares worship with profit and happiness, and wrongdoing with loss and ruin.

questions.question: What kind of teaching method is used in the passage?
questions.answer: It uses a story that teaches by comparison.

questions.question: Who are the main characters in the story?
questions.answer: Two soldiers.

questions.question: What common mission did both soldiers receive?
questions.answer: They were both sent to the same distant city.

questions.question: What important place did they reach during the journey?
questions.answer: They reached a fork where one road became two.

questions.question: Why was the man at the fork important?
questions.answer: He warned them about the outcomes of both choices.

questions.question: What good things were connected with the right-hand road?
questions.answer: Benefit, inner peace, and a good result for most travelers.

questions.question: What bad things were connected with the left-hand road?
questions.answer: No real gain and loss for most travelers.

questions.question: Why might some people still be tempted by the left-hand road?
questions.answer: Because it looked lighter and easier since there was no load to carry.

questions.question: What does this show about appearances?
questions.answer: Something can look easy on the outside while hiding harm inside.

questions.question: What was required from the soldier on the right road?
questions.answer: He had to accept order and carry his needed gear.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier who accepted that responsibility?
questions.answer: He was protected from fear and from depending on others.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier who refused that responsibility?
questions.answer: He suffered fear, need, and humiliation.

questions.question: What was the emotional state of the disobedient soldier during his trip?
questions.answer: He was anxious, pressured, and frightened.

questions.question: What was the emotional state of the obedient soldier during his trip?
questions.answer: He was calm, confident, and at peace.

questions.question: How did each soldier end his journey?
questions.answer: One was punished, and the other was rewarded.

questions.question: Why was the obedient soldier rewarded?
questions.answer: He carried out his duty faithfully and stayed within order.

questions.question: What does the passage say lies in worship?
questions.answer: Great gain and happiness.

questions.question: What does the passage say lies in vice and wasteful living?
questions.answer: Great loss and destruction.

questions.question: What job or role did the two men in the story have?
questions.answer: They were soldiers.

questions.question: Where were they supposed to go?
questions.answer: To a city far away.

questions.question: Before they chose a road, what help did they receive?
questions.answer: Someone explained the dangers and benefits of each road.

questions.question: Which road had rules and authority over it?
questions.answer: The road on the right.

questions.question: Which road had no rules and no one in charge?
questions.answer: The road on the left.

questions.question: What did the right-road travelers have to carry besides food?
questions.answer: A strong rifle.

questions.question: What was the first soldier willing to accept?
questions.answer: He was willing to carry a small burden and follow order.

questions.question: What did he gain by doing that?
questions.answer: He gained safety in his heart and freedom from depending on others.

questions.question: What was the second soldier unwilling to accept?
questions.answer: He did not want discipline or the load that came with it.

questions.question: What did he wrongly think he was gaining?
questions.answer: He thought he was gaining comfort and relief.

questions.question: What did he actually gain instead?
questions.answer: Heavy fear, neediness, and shame.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast outer load and inner load?
questions.answer: A small outer burden can save a person from a huge inner burden.

questions.question: What happened to the second soldier’s heart and spirit?
questions.answer: His heart became squeezed by worry, and his spirit was crushed by fear.

questions.question: What kind of person was the first soldier by the end?
questions.answer: An honorable soldier who had done his duty well.

questions.question: What kind of person was the second soldier by the end?
questions.answer: A rebel and deserter who faced punishment.

questions.question: What warning does the story give about rejecting rightful order?
questions.answer: Rejecting rightful order can bring misery even if it looks easy at first.

questions.question: What encouragement does the story give about worship and obedience?
questions.answer: They may seem hard at first, but they lead to peace, honor, and a good ending.

questions.question: At the start of the comparison, what are listeners told to understand?
questions.answer: They are told to understand that worship brings great good, while sinful behavior brings great harm.

questions.question: What moment forced the two soldiers to make a decision?
questions.answer: They reached a place where they had to choose between two roads.

questions.question: What did the guide say about the chances of success on the right side?
questions.answer: He said most who took it gained greatly and felt at ease.

questions.question: What did the guide say about the left side?
questions.answer: He said it gave no benefit and most who took it lost.

questions.question: What might make a careless person choose the left road?
questions.answer: The person might only notice the lighter load and ignore the danger.

questions.question: What did the successful soldier do after hearing the advice?
questions.answer: He chose the road on the right.

questions.question: What does that choice show about him?
questions.answer: It shows wisdom and willingness to accept responsibility.

questions.question: What kind of weight did he carry physically?
questions.answer: He carried a manageable amount of equipment.

questions.question: What kind of weight did he avoid emotionally?
questions.answer: He avoided overwhelming fear and dependence.

questions.question: What did the other soldier do after hearing the same advice?
questions.answer: He chose to leave the ordered path and go left.

questions.question: How did the left-road traveler act toward other people?
questions.answer: He had to ask others for help like a beggar.

questions.question: How did he react to things around him?
questions.answer: He was scared by everything he faced.

questions.question: What does this suggest about a life without discipline?
questions.answer: It can leave a person weak, worried, and unsteady.

questions.question: How did the obedient soldier travel emotionally?
questions.answer: With peace in his heart and conscience.

questions.question: Why was he not dependent on others?
questions.answer: He had obeyed and carried what he needed.

questions.question: Compare the ending of the two soldiers in one sentence.
questions.answer: The disobedient one ended in punishment, while the obedient one ended in reward.

questions.question: What four things are connected in the opening line of the passage?
questions.answer: Worship is linked with profit and happiness, while vice and wasteful living are linked with loss and ruin.

questions.question: What choice faced both soldiers?
questions.answer: They had to choose between two different roads.

questions.question: What did the speaker at the fork say about the right road’s outcome for most people?
questions.answer: Most people who took it did well and found peace.

questions.question: What did he say about the left road’s outcome for most people?
questions.answer: Most people who took it ended up harmed and without gain.

questions.question: What outer advantage did the left road seem to offer?
questions.answer: It seemed to offer comfort because there was nothing to carry.

questions.question: What hidden advantage did the right road offer?
questions.answer: It gave protection, order, and a good ending.

questions.question: What does the food carried on the right road suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests being prepared and provided for on the journey.

questions.question: What does the rifle carried on the right road suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests strength and protection against danger.

questions.question: How did the fortunate soldier treat the command he had been given?
questions.answer: He respected it and followed it.

questions.question: What happened to his inner life because of that?
questions.answer: His heart and spirit were kept safe from many heavy troubles.

questions.question: How did the other soldier treat the command?
questions.answer: He rejected it and broke away from order.

questions.question: What happened to him on the road because of that choice?
questions.answer: He became needy, frightened, and miserable.

questions.question: What does his begging show about the result of his choice?
questions.answer: It shows that trying to avoid a small burden led him into greater weakness.

questions.question: What does his fear of every object and event tell us?
questions.answer: It tells us he had no inner security.

questions.question: Why is the obedient soldier described as fearing no one?
questions.answer: Because he was prepared and was walking the proper path.

questions.question: What made him deserving of reward at the end?
questions.answer: He remained faithful to his duty all the way.

questions.question: What made the other soldier deserving of punishment?
questions.answer: He rebelled and deserted instead of obeying.

questions.question: If someone judges only by what feels lighter at first, which soldier is he thinking like?
questions.answer: He is thinking like the disobedient soldier.

questions.question: What overall truth does the passage teach about worship and sinful living?
questions.answer: Worship may ask for effort, but it leads to peace and success, while sinful living may look easy but ends in harm.
